standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the four functors F_iso, F_inj, F_surj and F_zero whose sheaf and limit preserving properties are asserted.

standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness of an fpqc covering and faithful flatness of the induced local maps
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Topologies, label topologies-lemma-fpqc (proof line 5937); Algebra, label algebra-lemma-local-flat-ff (proof line 5942)
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the pullback covering of X_T is an fpqc covering, so every point has a point of some member over it, and that the resulting local map of stalks is faithfully flat, which is what makes injectivity, surjectivity, bijectivity and vanishing equivalent upstairs and downstairs.

standard_prerequisites.name: The algebraic colimit statements for module maps and reduction of finite type and finite presentation modules
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, label algebra-lemma-module-map-property-in-colimit, parts (1), (2) and (3), invoked at proof lines 5975, 5987 and 6004; Properties, labels properties-lemma-finite-type-module (proof line 5966) and properties-lemma-finite-presentation-module (proof line 5994)
standard_prerequisites.use: Each of the limit preserving parts is reduced to the corresponding algebraic statement that surjectivity, vanishing or bijectivity of a base changed map descends to some stage of a directed colimit, and the reduction from sheaves to modules uses the affine local description of a finite type or finite presentation module.

core_obligations: Prove the sheaf property: the pullback of an fpqc covering to X_T is an fpqc covering, so for every point x of X_T there is an index i and a point x_i over x; since the local map of stalks is faithfully flat, the map u_i at x_i is injective, surjective, bijective or zero exactly when u_T is at x, which gives all four functors at once (proof lines 5934-5945).

Prove that F_surj is limit preserving: for a directed limit over which u_T is surjective, cover the quasi-compact X_{i_0} by finitely many affine opens mapping into affine opens of X, reduce to showing surjectivity of one restriction at some stage, and translate the resulting algebraic problem into the colimit statement for surjectivity of a module map with finite target (proof lines 5947-5975).

Prove that F_zero is limit preserving by literally the same reduction, leading to the colimit statement for a module map that becomes zero after base change with finite source (proof lines 5977-5987).

Prove that F_iso is limit preserving by the same reduction, with the extra use of the finite presentation description of G, leading to the colimit statement that an isomorphism after base change descends to a stage when the source is finite and the target finitely presented (proof lines 5989-6004).
proof_roadmap: Sheaf property from faithful flatness of the local maps of stalks induced by an fpqc covering (proof lines 5934-5945).
Reduce each limit preserving statement to a finite affine covering and then to an algebraic colimit statement for module maps (proof lines 5947-6004).
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the four functors recording that a module map becomes injective, surjective, bijective or zero satisfy the fpqc sheaf property, and that the surjectivity, vanishing and bijectivity functors are limit preserving under the stated finiteness hypotheses (statement lines 5918-5931, tag 05MJ). The sheaf part is a short faithful flatness argument on stalks, but the limit preserving parts require a real reduction each: the quasi-compact source is covered by finitely many affine opens mapping into affine opens of the base, the question is turned into one about a module map over a directed colimit of algebras, and the three cases are then matched to the corresponding algebraic colimit statements. The reduction scheme is uniform but must be carried out three times with the right finiteness hypothesis each time, so the claim is H2.
